relevance_note: Case report of two Iranian boys with infantile Alexander disease and heterozygous GFAP variants: "Genetic study revealed a heterozygous mutation of p.Arg79His in the exon 1 of GFAP gene".
method_note: Hand-built from a short text and Table 1 (patients as rows; label column 'Patient' with values 1 and 2; the text calls them 'Case 1'/'Case 2', used as labels per rule 1). Table 1 'Nucleotide change' prints '716G > A' and '236G > A' without a 'c.' prefix or transcript; recorded as printed in variant_original_string and cdna_hgvs_as_stated. Table 1 column 'Degradation' (7mo, 6mo) read as age at developmental regression; for Case 1 this matches the text (regression after the seizure at 7 months); for Case 2 the 6mo cell is the only age for regression. MRI: the per-case figure legends give individual findings (periventricular rim, frontal white matter involvement; subependymal cysts for case 1 only). The four-item criteria list ('Based on following criteria, AD diagnosis in our patients was wstablished') is stated for 'our patients' (both cases) and is recorded with evidence_basis 'inferred from group statement'; the fifth criterion that was not met is not named, so contrast enhancement is not reported. Brain stem/midbrain abnormality is not mapped to the medulla/cervical cord checklist item. Case 1 normal metabolic tests recorded as excluded abnormalities per D-27; Case 2 'Laboratory tests similar to the first patient, were all within normal limit' recorded as one generic exclusion (tests not named for Case 2). Developmental regression is not treated as developmental delay or cognitive decline; Case 1 attained head holding at 7 months, but the paper does not call this delay, so not recorded. is_proband null: neither is called proband/index case and the report has two patients. Contradiction: the abstract and introduction say 'We report two novel mutations too in the GFAP gene', while the discussion says 'Both the p.Arg239His and p.Arg79His coding changes have been previously associated with AD patients'; novelty is not recorded. Pathogenicity for Case 2's p.Arg79His taken from 'The p.Arg79His mutation is considered causative for AxD due to its de novo appearance' (a statement about the variant attributed to ref [6]; it is not parental testing for Case 2, so inheritance is not reported). No parental testing reported for either case.
